notes: HamsterHourToken is a plain OpenZeppelin ERC-20 with no constructor arguments: 1,000,000,000 HAMSTER at 18 decimals minted once to msg.sender (the launch factory). No owner, mint, burn, pause, blacklist, transfer fee or upgrade path; a transfer always moves the full amount. AntiSniperHook is an immutable buy-fee hook for the HAMSTER/IMD pool. Constructor, in declaration order: IPoolManager manager_ ($poolManager), address hamster_ ($token), uint256 startBps_ = 3000, uint256 floorBps_ = 500, uint256 decaySeconds_ = 600, address feeRecipient_ = 0xbb85c1b7540d9e7b56f7a595fc1ff7dd07cb0823 (the brief's literal FEE_RECIPIENT, which is also the launch owner). The constructor reverts if any of the four economic arguments differs from src/DeploymentConfig.sol or if any address is zero, and it records poolInitialisedAt = block.timestamp. The hook has no owner, setter, pause, rescue or sweep, so there is no $owner argument; the fee recipient has no function to call. getHookPermissions returns beforeInitialize, beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta and afterSwapReturnDelta (address mask 0x20cc). beforeInitialize accepts only the PoolManager as caller, only the pool key (HAMSTER, IMD 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7, LP fee 12500, tickSpacing 60, this hook) and only in the same block timestamp as the hook's deployment: the factory must deploy the hook and call PoolManager.initialize in one transaction, which is how the launch factory works. It does not check the initializing sender, so no $factory argument is needed. Fee: on a buy (swap input is IMD) the hook takes feeBps of the gross IMD input, decaying linearly from 3000 bps at t=0 to 500 bps at t>=600 s (1750 bps at t=300 s) and staying at 500 bps forever; sells (input is HAMSTER) and plain transfers are never taxed. Exact-input buys are charged in beforeSwap via a positive specified delta; exact-output buys are grossed up in afterSwap via a positive unspecified delta. The fee is paid inside the swap by poolManager.take(IMD, FEE_RECIPIENT, fee) and never passes through the hook, which holds no funds. The LP fee is the pool's own 12500 (1.25%) and the hook never overrides it (returns 0 as lpFeeOverride). It declares no liquidity callbacks, so the factory's zero-liquidity fee collect is untouched. pool.initialPrice is written as the launch facts give it; the deployer derives the opening price from the 2,500 IMD opening market cap and the token address. Caveat recorded in README: because the fee is transferred from the PoolManager's IMD balance during the swap, a router that settles its input only after the swap can fail on a manager holding too little IMD; a router that settles its IMD budget before calling swap (test/helpers/PoolDriver.sol) always succeeds.
